note: Test keys, derived from the issuer's name. Never credentials.

cases.name: one statement
cases.about: A mandate holds what it lists, and nothing else was ever held.

cases.name: canonical bytes
cases.about: A reason with characters outside ASCII, quotation marks and a tab. Characters outside ASCII are written as they are, in UTF-8; the quotation mark, the backslash and control characters are escaped. For this body that is RFC 8785.

cases.name: supersession
cases.about: A later statement replaces the earlier one whole.

cases.name: revocation
cases.about: A statement with no contracts ends the mandate from the instant it was issued, and not before.

cases.name: expiry
cases.about: A statement stops holding at expires_at_ms, with no further statement. The instant itself is outside.

cases.name: renewal
cases.about: Renewed before it expired: the first expiry no longer applies.

cases.name: forged: unknown issuer
cases.about: Well formed and well signed by someone the site does not know. Ignored; the withdrawal stands.

cases.name: forged: wrong key
cases.about: In a trusted issuer's name, signed with another key. Ignored.

cases.name: forged: altered
cases.about: A real statement changed after it was signed, with a matching id. Ignored.

cases.name: forged: id does not match
cases.about: The body was changed and the id was not. The only statement does not count, so nothing is established.

cases.name: forged withdrawal
cases.about: A withdrawal by someone the site does not know takes nothing away.

cases.name: another principal
cases.about: A statement for someone else is not read for this one.

cases.name: fork
cases.about: Two statements that count supersede the same one. Authority is not established: refuse.

statements.reason: a second statement on the same one

cases.name: broken chain
cases.about: A statement that counts supersedes one that is not there. Not established.

cases.name: nothing counts
cases.about: Only a forgery was presented. Not established.

cases.name: delegation
cases.about: The orchestrator passes its mandate on. The agent holds what both statements list, and never what the orchestrator did not hold.

statements.reason: the orchestrator passes on more than it holds

cases.name: delegation: the giver's mandate is withdrawn
cases.about: When the orchestrator's mandate ends, so does what it passed on, with no statement about the agent.

statements.reason: the orchestrator passes on more than it holds

cases.name: delegation: the giver's mandate expires
cases.about: Passed on for a minute by someone who holds it for five seconds: five seconds.

cases.name: delegation: the giver has no statements
cases.about: Passed on by someone for whom nothing is established. Not established.

statements.reason: the orchestrator passes on more than it holds

cases.name: delegation: not marked as one
cases.about: The orchestrator signs a mandate of its own. It is not an issuer the site trusts to do that, so the statement does not count.

statements.reason: the orchestrator gives a mandate of its own

cases.name: delegation: a loop
cases.about: Each passes on to the other and nobody was given anything. Not established.

cases.name: rotation
cases.about: The old key signed before it was retired and the new key after. Both count.

cases.name: rotation: the retired key signs afterwards
cases.about: Well signed with a key that had been rotated out when it was issued. Ignored.

cases.name: rotation: the new key, dated before it was valid
cases.about: A key signs only from the instant it is valid. Ignored.

cases.name: standing ended: what was given before stays
cases.about: An issuer who has left does not take back what it gave while it had standing.

cases.name: standing ended: a statement issued afterwards
cases.about: Well signed with the issuer's own key after its standing ended. Ignored.

cases.name: an unsigned withdrawal
cases.about: A withdrawal with no signature: someone says the mandate was withdrawn. It does not count, so the mandate is held as before. A withdrawal is evidence only when it is signed.

cases.name: dated back: first seen after the key was retired
cases.about: Signed with a retired key and dated one millisecond before it was retired. By its own date it would count. The site first saw it at 4000, after the key was retired at 3000, so it does not.

cases.name: the same statement, seen in time
cases.about: The same bytes, first seen at 2999 while the key was valid. It counts, and what the key signed while it was valid stays after the key is retired.

cases.name: a statement the site has not seen
cases.about: With times of first sight given, a statement that is not among them does not count, whatever it says.
